clue.text: One so uptight could be a deal strict

indicators.note: says the letters of the following words could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A prim person might well be thought rather strict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' signals the anagram of A DEAL STRICT; 'One so' merely introduces the person described.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prim and rigidly proper is tense and uptight about conduct.

clue.text: Vulnerable to a point of issue

definitions.meaning: liable or exposed to something, as in 'prone to colds'
the topic or matter under discussion

explanation.definitionFit: Being liable to something is being exposed to it; the matter under debate is the theme or topic.

clue.text: Show of unusual entertainment initially

parts.note: something unusual is rare

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of the word entertainment

explanation.surface: A display of out-of-the-ordinary entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: A raree show was a travelling peepshow; the word alone stands for the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A raree, short for raree-show, was a street peepshow carried in a box, a type of show.

clue.text: When and where to find an agenda item recorded

definitions.text: where to find an agenda item recorded
definitions.meaning: a meeting's decisions are written up in its official minutes

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'very soon', and literally places a recorded item inside the minutes of a meeting.

clue.text: Herald different only in Scotland

indicators.note: the word only is made different by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: An official messenger who is unlike others only north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Scotland' narrows the definition: the Lord Lyon King of Arms is Scotland's chief herald.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Lyon King of Arms heads heraldry in Scotland, so the title names a herald.

clue.text: Sit back on a moving camel for traveller's joy

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, so on joins them in this order
the camel is moving, so its letters are shifted about
Sit is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

explanation.surface: A rider settles onto a camel on the move, delighting the traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns CAMEL into CLEMA; 'back' turns SIT into TIS; 'on' puts CLEMA above TIS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Traveller's joy is the common name of a wild climbing plant of the genus with that Latin name.

clue.text: Where the lawman takes tea in Russia

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American lawman
CHA is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: A lawyer stops for a cup of tea while in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Russia' qualifies 'Where': a dacha is a Russian country house. CHA is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian country cottage is a place where someone stays.

clue.text: New game set in Wales

indicators.note: a new version of the words game set has its letters arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A fresh round of tennis is played in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Maesteg is a town in south Wales; 'in Wales' stands for a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies in the Llynfi valley of Glamorgan, a place in that country.

clue.text: One who always speaks well of the dead

definitions.text: One who always speaks well of the dead

parts.words: One who always speaks well of the dead
parts.note: describes the person delivering praise at a funeral, whose job is to speak well of the deceased

explanation.surface: A kindly soul who never says a bad word about the departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A person giving a funeral tribute praises the deceased by its nature.

clue.text: Song for girl in the altogether!

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: in the altogether means naked, so bare
Carol is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A tune for a young woman who is stark naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the altogether' is British slang for nude, giving BARE around CAROL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian gondolier's song, or music imitating one, is a type of song.

clue.text: Reason union leader entered the cabinet

indicators.note: one part goes into another, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a cabinet is a display case

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A trade-union boss walks into a government cabinet meeting with his argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive or ground for something is its reason.

clue.text: Overseer in the temple area

parts.note: reads 'over-seer' as something over the organ of sight, found near the side of the head

explanation.surface: A supervisor working in a religious building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temple' looks religious, but it is the side of the head; the 'overseer' is what covers the seeing organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin covering the eye sits close to the temple on the face.

clue.text: Deal vigorously with a loafer

definitions.meaning: to hit out at them on all sides
an idle person who avoids work

explanation.definitionFit: To lay about means to strike out vigorously; joined into one word it names an idler.

clue.text: Place to get trains to Britain in Libya

parts.note: BR is British Rail, which ran the UK's trains
UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Libya where you catch trains back to Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Libya' qualifies 'Place': Tobruk is a Libyan port, besieged in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobruk is a port city in Libya, so a place there.

clue.text: He gets credit from a Romany-loving author hesitantly

parts.note: George Borrow wrote about Romany life in Lavengro and The Romany Rye
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A man is given credit by a writer fond of Gypsies who stammers.
explanation.walkthrough: George Borrow was a 19th-century English writer who travelled with the Romany people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes a loan is given credit by a lender.

clue.text: Do wrong cooking in egg and burning it!

parts.note: to sin is to do wrong

indicators.note: cooking suggests the words in egg are worked into a new mix

explanation.surface: Messing up the cookery and scorching the egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges IN EGG into GEING, which follows SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorching something lightly at the surface is burning it.

clue.text: Act the dandy around tea-time

indicators.note: the first word goes around the second

parts.note: a gallant is a fashionable young man, a dandy
four o'clock, written IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Behave like a fop at about four in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea-time is taken as four o'clock, IV, placed inside GALLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To gad about seeking pleasure is a way to behave, loosely to act.

clue.text: Muse on the vision of Sir Robin?

indicators.note: the vision belonging to Sir Robin puts his name before the word for vision

parts.note: Sir Robin Day was a famous British political broadcaster
a dream is a vision

explanation.surface: Pondering what a knight called Robin saw in his sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Robin Day was a British TV interviewer, famous for his bow tie.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to be lost in idle thought, like a reverie.

clue.text: Cheese for the crocked spare man

indicators.note: crocked means injured or broken, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Food for the injured reserve player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crocked' is British for injured; here it scrambles SPARE MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese.

clue.text: Making a hit with a wallpapering job

definitions.meaning: applying glue to the back of wallpaper before hanging it

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a heavy beating and the task of gluing wallpaper.

clue.text: Criticised over roof repairs?

definitions.meaning: a roof repaired with stone tiles is covered in them

explanation.definitionFit: To be harshly reviewed is to be panned; a roof covered with stone tiles has been tiled that way.

clue.text: Compensation ladies take in silver

indicators.note: the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: dames are ladies
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Women accept silver as recompense.
explanation.definitionFit: Money awarded by a court for loss or injury is compensation.

clue.text: Barrier giving goods a boost, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the following sounds like the words given

parts.note: goods are stock, and a boost is aid, giving stock aid

explanation.surface: A fence that gives a lift to merchandise, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensive wall of upright stakes is a barrier.

clue.text: Knight let out got down to it

parts.note: KN is an abbreviation for knight

indicators.note: out shows the word let is jumbled

explanation.surface: A knight released went down to business.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down onto one's knees, as to pray, is kneeling.

clue.text: Anyhow, one dram's enough to entrance

indicators.note: anyhow means in a haphazard way, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A single drink will be enough to bewitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb, to charm, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone so they lose their hostility is to enchant or win them over.

clue.text: Comrade I'm backing in an attempt

indicators.note: one part is placed inside another

parts.note: an is A and an attempt is a go

indicators.note: the word I'm is read backwards

explanation.surface: A friend says he supports an effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, a pal or comrade.

clue.text: One man's career can be a drag, note

parts.note: to lug is to drag
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A man's working life can be a bore, observe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' means a headlong rush, not a profession: a luge is a one-person sled.
explanation.definitionFit: A small toboggan for a single rider careers down the track.

clue.text: A Forsyte showing anger on Wearside

parts.note: ire is anger
Wearside, around Sunderland, is in the North East of England

explanation.surface: A member of the Forsyte family loses her temper in Sunderland.
explanation.walkthrough: Irene is a character in Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga; Wearside is the Sunderland area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a character in Galsworthy's Forsyte novels, a member of that family by marriage.

clue.text: Following the example of language used in Oriental attack

parts.note: E stands for eastern

indicators.note: one part is put to use inside another

parts.note: to mug is to attack
Latin is a language

explanation.surface: Copying the tongue spoken during an Eastern raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying someone is imitating them, modelling oneself on them.

clue.text: Seems put out when agitated

indicators.note: agitated shakes up the letters of the words before

explanation.surface: Someone appears upset when stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and also the anagram of SEEMS PUT OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stormy and turbulent means looking upset and stirred up.
